sentences.text: 1 This appeal is filed by the claimant being aggrieved of award dated 28/01/2022 passed by the learned 15t h Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in Claim Case No. 2693/2019 on the ground that the Tribunal has not treated son of the deceased to be dependent and has awarded only a sum of Rs. 70,000/- under the head of loss of estate, last rites etc. after calculating compensation of Rs. 8,68,660/-.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Reliance is placed on the decision of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Birender and others I (2020) ACC 130 (SC).

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Birender and others I (2020) ACC 130 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In para 15, it is held that even major sons are legal representatives of the deceased and have a right to apply for the compensation.

In view of such facts,
the impugned award needs to be modified.
It appears that the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the ratio of the law laid down by the Supreme Court i n Birender (supra) and has acted in an arbitrary and illegal manner.
Accordingly, the impugned award is modified.
It is directed that claimant will be entitled to calculated amount of Rs. 8,68,660/- along with 7% interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
The liability will be joint and several against all the non-appellants as no breach of policy could be proved by the Insurance Company.
In above terms, the appeal is allowed and disposed of.
Record of the Tribunal be sent back.
Later on, Shri Gulab Chand Sohane, learned counsel appears for respondent no. 3 and prays for marking his presence.
His presence is marked.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE vy Vinod Khare vs Pramod Kumar Sen on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108488818/
